title: Advisory observation
description: One vendor technology, one observed behaviour or one published exposure, one source. The six top-level keys map to the six questions the corpus answers: who, what, how, where, who2, when. record_type decides which of the two shapes a record takes.

id.description: Stable slug. obs- prefix for observations, exp- prefix for exposures.

record_type.description: observation = something was seen happening; carries detection logic in how[]; written by hand from a source. exposure = a product is affected by a named vulnerability; carries no detection logic; generated in bulk from a vulnerability advisory. Observations answer 'what should I watch for'. Exposures answer 'what has been published about my kit'. The lookup ranks observations first and returns exposures as a separate block, so that a few thousand exposures cannot bury the observations.

status.description: seed = written from general knowledge, source URL not yet re-read. verified = a human or a fetch confirmed the source says this.

who.description: The vendor technology the scenario is about.

products.description: Canonical product names. Aliases live in aliases.json, not here.

product_class.description: One or more vocab product_class values. This is what answers 'I have a firewall' when the vendor is not the one in the record.

versions_affected.description: Free text as the source stated it.

what.description: What was observed happening to or through this technology.

role.description: Vocab role. What part the technology played in the scenario.

summary.description: Plain prose, as short as the scenario allows and rarely more than a few sentences. No marketing language, no hedging. The one-sentence form this field once demanded is met by 209 of 1,151 records and was never enforced, so the contract is brevity and plainness rather than a sentence count.

attack_surface.description: Vocab attack_surface value. Where the exposure sat.

how.description: How the activity was or can be observed. Each entry is one detection idea, shaped so it can be converted to Cortex XQL later. Mandatory for record_type observation, where at least one entry is required; validate.py enforces that. Normally absent on record_type exposure, which asserts that a product is affected rather than describing anything observed. An exposure may carry a how block only where the advisory itself published detection guidance.

pattern_id.description: Optional link into patterns.jsonl. Two records sharing a pattern_id are the same detection scenario across different technologies. This is the grouping mechanism.

evidence_type.description: Vocab evidence_type values. What telemetry is needed.

dataset_hint.description: Likely Cortex dataset names, e.g. cisco_asa_raw. A hint, not a guarantee it is onboarded.

logic.description: The detection stated in plain words, precisely enough that an engineer could write the query from it alone.

fields.description: The concrete field tests. Each becomes a filter clause.

xdm.description: XDM field path where one is known.

raw.description: Raw vendor field or log token.

iocs.description: Atomic indicators. Low shelf life. Kept because they are cheap to query, not because they are durable.

fidelity.description: alert = specific enough to page someone. hunt = needs an analyst. enrich = context only.

confidence.description: Confidence that this logic reflects what the source actually described.

caveat.description: Known false positive source or coverage gap. Say it here rather than leaving it implied.

rule_shape.description: Vocab rule_shape value. Tells a rule generator what query structure the markers need.

locus.description: Optional declared override for the computed LOCUS. Omit it. The label is derived from attack_surface, product_class and evidence_type, and a hand-set value that agrees with the derivation is a value that will silently stop agreeing when the derivation changes. Set it only where the derivation is provably wrong for this block, and say why in notes.

markers.description: Clean, literal, rule-generatable observables drawn from the source. Unlike 'fields' these carry a controlled type and must be concrete enough to compile into a query.

value.description: Literal observable, or array for match=in.

xdm.description: XDM field this marker binds to, where one exists.

expr.description: Mandatory when type is computed: the computation to perform.

where.description: Where the knowledge came from. Public sources carry a url. Licensed sources carry disclosure=restricted and an abstract citation instead; see corpus/README.md for the abstraction rule.

source_id.description: Stable slug for the source, so several observations can cite the same article. For restricted sources this must not encode the publisher's report identifier.

title.description: For restricted sources: an abstract citation of the form '<Publisher> commentary on <subject>'. Never the publisher's own report title or report number.

url.description: Public sources only. Omit for restricted sources; there is nothing a reader could open.

disclosure.description: public = anyone can read the source at the url. restricted = licensed or subscriber intelligence. Restricted records must carry no report identifier, no verbatim wording, and no url.

retrieved.description: ISO date the source was last read.

verified.description: False means the source has not been re-read since the record was written.

corroborations.description: Independent public accounts of the same thing, beyond the primary source. Originally added so a record whose primary source is restricted could still be verified by a reader without access to it, and now also the place a second or third publisher on one mechanism goes -- a further account is an entry here, never a near-duplicate record. Was two flat strings until 0.19.0; a third publisher had nowhere to go, and two parallel lists would have had to stay index-aligned by hand.

url.description: Public URL for it. Public by definition -- a corroboration that cannot be read corroborates nothing.

who2.description: Who was behind it and who was on the receiving end.

actors.description: Every name the source used, including aliases from other vendors.

observed_start.description: ISO date or partial date (YYYY, YYYY-MM, YYYY-MM-DD).

notes.description: Anything an analyst should know that no other field carries.
